newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end sharply off, properties slump.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end sharply off, properties slump.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended sharply lower on Tuesday, dragged down by weak futures and continued selling pressure on the property sector.
The Hang Seng Index fell 189.33 points, or 1.39 percent, to close at 13,454.21.

"The rally before Chinese New Year was a little bit overdone," said Sunny Chan, senior research manager at Seapower Securities. "People are worried about the impact of any further measures to curb property speculation and some investors are interpreting the strong U.S. dollar against the Hong Kong dollar as some foreign funds leaving the Hong Kong market."
Tuesday's turnover was HK$7.57 billion compared with HK$7.63 billion on Monday.
The U.S. dollar stood at HK$7.7445/55 on Tuesday after touching HK$7.75 last week for the first time since January 1995. The rate usually ranges between HK$7.73 to HK$7.74.
Brokers said investors had hoped for a rally following the Chinese New Year holiday and bid prices up beforehand. The Hang Seng rose 2.54 percent during last week's three trading days.
"Today is just a continuation of yesterday. Traders had hoped to flip stock into the New Year rally and it didn't materialise," said one trader at a U.S. brokerage firm.
"In the game of pass the parcel, the music has stopped. There is no next buyer, as yet," he added.
February Hang Seng index futures closed 180 points lower at 13,380. Brokers said they had led the market's decline.
"They dropped before the cash market. They are trading at a substantial discount to the cash market," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager Nikko Securities.
Some property stocks took a beating as investors remained concerned about the impact of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's recommendation to limit mortgage lending for luxury properties.
Sun Hung Kai Properties tumbled HK$2.75 to HK$88.25 and Henderson Land fell HK$1.50 to HK$70.00.
"We may have to wait until some major developers release some properties for sale to see the impact of these measures," said Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International.
He said Hong Kong stocks may weaken further. "We may see further consolidation between 13,000 and 13,500."
HSBC Holdings fell HK$2.50 to HK$187.00 and Hang Seng Bank slumped HK$2.00 to HK$91.50.
Giordano jumped HK$0.525 to HK$5.00 after recent weakness.
